title: Building to flip is building to flop
coreMove: Build a company worth running, not one staged for sale; let customer value pick your priorities, because designing for an acquirer pulls the first decisions toward the wrong audience.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders planning the sale before the first release
exampleSpecs.stakes: aim the roadmap at an acquirer or at a customer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist chooses commitment strategy over exit strategy

exampleSpecs.audience: teams unsure whether staying independent is a real strategy
exampleSpecs.stakes: treat independence as an accident or as a deliberate posture
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist frames commitment as an operating stance

exampleSpecs.audience: founders conflating buyer appeal with customer value
exampleSpecs.stakes: chase numbers a buyer rewards or value a customer rewards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates keeping buyers happy from keeping customers happy

exampleSpecs.audience: makers mistaking exit fluency for discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: read exit fluency as discipline or as detachment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist reads exit talk as a sign of premature absence

exampleSpecs.audience: competent teams building only to flip
exampleSpecs.stakes: build as a stepping stone or invest real care
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist traces a hollow product back to its stepping-stone motive

exampleSpecs.audience: owners who think commitment forbids ever selling
exampleSpecs.stakes: refuse a fair offer on principle or judge it on merit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist distinguishes building-to-flip from a sensible sale
